assessment_summary: The statement claims convergence in distribution implies convergence in probability. This is false unless the limit is a constant. We can construct a counterexample where X_n and X have the same distribution (and thus trivially converge in distribution) but are anti-correlated, meaning the distance between them is always large.
counterexample: Let the probability space be a fair coin flip, so Omega = {H, T} with probability 1/2 each. Let X(H) = 1 and X(T) = 0. Let X_n(H) = 0 and X_n(T) = 1 for all n. Both X and X_n have a Bernoulli(1/2) distribution. Since X_n has the exact same distribution as X for all n, X_n converges to X in distribution. However, |X_n - X| is always 1, so P(|X_n - X| > 0.5) = 1 for all n, which does not converge to 0. Thus X_n does not converge to X in probability.
